aboutSections.title: How sections work
aboutSections.intro: Bitsocial Forum is split into sections, one for each area of Bitsocial: the protocol, the BSO token and Bitsocial Chain, each app, the anti-spam challenges, the bots and the infrastructure. This page explains what a section is and who runs it.

community.title: Each section is a community
community.body: A section's topics live in a Bitsocial community: a peer-to-peer space with its own moderators, rules and anti-spam challenges. The forum shows that community's topics under the section's name. The forum itself has no admins: it only decides which sections exist.

whoRuns.title: Who runs a section
whoRuns.body: The moderators of the community that holds it, and only for that section. The people who maintain pkc-js can run the protocol section without any say over the 5chan section, and each section sets its own rules, tags and anti-spam settings.

whyNotOne.title: Why not one community for the whole forum
whyNotOne.body: A single community would make whoever holds its key the admin of every discussion, which is what Bitsocial is built to avoid. Separate communities keep each project in charge of its own space, and keep the rest of the forum working if one of them goes offline.

changingHands.title: How a section changes hands
changingHands.body: Every section has a ranked list of candidate communities, and the top one is the one you see at the section's address. Today the list is kept by the forum's maintainers; the plan is for votes to rank candidates, the way 5chan's boards are ranked. If another community takes over a section, nothing is deleted: the previous community keeps its address, topics and members, and links to its topics keep working.

startCommunity.title: Starting a community for a section
startCommunity.body: Anyone can create a Bitsocial community, for example with Seedit or bitsocial-cli, and ask for it to be listed as a candidate for a section. Until voting exists, propose it in the General & meta section.

tags.title: Tags inside a section
tags.body: Topics are tagged with the project they are about or the kind of topic, such as a question, a bug or a proposal. Click a tag to see only those topics.

aboutSections.learnMoreBody: Sections are built on directories, the design Seedit and 5chan use to let communities compete for board names. The Bitsocial docs explain the technical side.
